text: One hosted instance for the whole house: accounts decide read or write, for UI and MCP alike
description:
Felix 2026-10-16. One Aimparency instance on a server Felix controls serves Commons Hub: residents, volunteers and guests. Access is to the instance (the backend), not per MCP: the backend enforces it for every client, and MCP clients authenticate through the UI (MCP OAuth: the client opens the instance's login page, gets a token).
- Accounts are configurable per project and kept out of git (e.g. .bowman/secrets.json, already gitignored), password hashes only.
- Write account: may change the graph. Changes stay as files on the server; someone with write access to the repository reviews and commits them by hand. Everyone with repo write access is responsible for keeping out changes that should not go in.
- Read-only: no change to anything checked in. Optionally behind a password too (guests).
- Propose for review is an extra, later: stored locally on the server (gitignored), never in the idea.
Parked first attempt: git stash 'parked: review-only access level + idea.proposeReview' (file marker instead of accounts; proposeReview wrote into the idea, which this design rejects). Its access-level guard can be reused, with the level coming from the session.

status.comment: Implemented in 7d73c932. pnpm start asks once for the repository, hosting, port, listen address and first admin; hosted mode serves the UI, /trpc and /mcp/sse on one port. Roles read (anyone), write, admin; one backend access middleware for UI and MCP; local-only tools are off when hosted. Tests: backend auth and hosted-server tests, validate-local-runtime, pnpm check 25/25. Waiting for Felix's trial on the Commons Hub server.
